title: Quick Play Guide
story: Congratulations! You are hired as the project manager. In this row you will learn the relevant part of the story of the particular space.
action_description: This row will summarise the actions that may need to be done to progress the game.
outcome_description: And this row is items chosen by chance… but not always because you can reject lady luck and NEGOTIATE.
can_negotiate: and if you really really really do not like your choices... Sometimes you can refuse them and just try again.

title: Strategy Guide
story: Now that you read the first column and know the rules - here is your strategy guide:
action_description: You just got hired by an owner. The 2 of you will dream up / design / review and build a project.
outcome_description: Strategise and pick the right dice rolls
can_negotiate: Don't forget waiting 1 extra turn if the roll is really bad may be more advantageous.

title: The owner walks you through it
story: Sit down. I've been turning this project over for months — let me walk you through what I want built. You're going to hear it from me first, before anyone else gets a say.
action_description: Lock the scope as offered, or push back and revisit tomorrow.

title: The owner opens the books
story: Here's what I'm putting in — {fundingAmount}. Look it over. I'm not negotiating against myself — but if you've got a real reason to push back, I'll hear it.
action_description: Take the check, or push for more and revisit tomorrow.
outcome_description: Owner's funding is in. Starting budget is set.

title: I pick a direction
story: I'm picking a direction. Expeditor and I have talked it through, but the call's mine. Time to commit.
action_description: Trim the team, see how the days shake out, commit to a path.
outcome_description: Direction set. Tomorrow I move on it.

title: I rethink the plan
story: Rethinking the plan. Life's moving fast, my staff's restless, and the first try didn't pan out.
action_description: A staff member quits for a better gig. Days pass. Commit to a new plan.
outcome_description: New direction locked. Time to act.

title: I'm flipping through your plan
story: Sit down. I've got your plan in front of me — let's see if it holds up. I'll cut you a rate, but I want my pound of flesh on the scope first.
action_description: Negotiate scope and rate. Lock in the terms, or push for better.
outcome_description: Terms agreed. On to the bank.

title: You again. Already.
story: You're back. Cash didn't last? Sit down — I'll listen, but the warmth's gone. This round it's whatever I'm willing to put up. You take it.
action_description: Re-pitch the ask. Take whatever the lender offers this time.

title: We're underwriting your file
story: We've got your file. Underwriting will work the numbers — amount, rate, timeline. We'll come back with terms. Standard process. Sit tight.
action_description: Sign the loan terms, or push for a lower rate.
outcome_description: Loan approved at the bank's terms. Money incoming.

title: We see you're back
story: You're back with us. We've already underwritten this project once for {fundingAmount} — second pass means a closer look and a tighter rate. Patience is shorter on this side too.
action_description: A banker stops returning your calls. Take the revised loan, whatever it looks like.
outcome_description: New terms in hand. Whatever they are.

title: The committee will hear you out
story: The committee will hear you out. We're slower than the bank and we cost more — but we move real money when we like the deal. Walk us through it.
action_description: Sign with the investors, or push for better terms.

title: The committee's seen you before
story: You're back. We've already put real money into this project once ({fundingAmount}) — the appetite for sweetening terms is gone. Take what we offer this round, or come back later.
action_description: An investor contact gets pulled into another deal. Take whatever terms come back.
outcome_description: Took what the committee offered. Moving on.

title: Hunting for an architect
story: I'm hunting for an architect. Calls, resumes, interviews — it takes days. I'd rather be building.
action_description: Work the phones. See who turns up.

title: I want another look at these drawings
story: I've been thinking about these drawings overnight and something's off. Give me another pass — I think we can do better. Push back if you have to, but I'd rather get this right than fast.
action_description: Accept the redesign, or push back on the changes.

title: Let's talk about my fee
story: We need to talk money. I've put real time into this — sketches, options, conversations with the consultants. The fee covers the work I've already done. It's not unreasonable.
action_description: Cut a contact to save budget. Pay the fee, or push back.
outcome_description: Fee agreed. Moving to the design work.

title: There's more to the work than I quoted
story: The scope grew. It always does. The original fee covered the original drawings — what's been added needs to be paid for separately. I'm not nickel-and-diming. This is the actual extra work.
action_description: Pay the extra, or push back on the upcharge.

title: Today is the design reveal
story: Today's the day. We've finished the design — every elevation, every section, every detail. Sit through the presentation, then we'll talk about whether it's ready for engineering.
action_description: Watch the presentation. Approve the design, or send it back.

title: Here's the revised design
story: Took your feedback. Here are the revised drawings — I think you'll see the changes. If they don't land, send it back again, but I'd rather we converge this round.
action_description: Compare the new drawings to the old. Approve the revisions, or send them back again.

title: Hunting for an engineer
story: I'm hunting for a structural engineer. Same grind as the architect — calls, credentials, interviews.
action_description: Work the phones. See who turns up.

title: I need another pass at the calcs
story: I've been over the structural calculations and I want another pass. Numbers don't lie — if something's off, we fix it now, before steel orders or pour schedules. I'd rather slow down here than have it back at me later.
action_description: Accept the engineer's findings, or ask for another pass.

title: Let's settle the fee
story: Let's settle the fee. Structural is precise work — load calcs, code review, stamped drawings. The number reflects the liability I carry on this. I don't pad it.
action_description: Every penny counts. Pay the fee, or push back.
outcome_description: Fee settled. On to the design.

title: More work, more fee
story: Scope grew. Load calcs need redoing. Either you pay for the additional engineering, or we sign off on what's already there — and I don't recommend that.
action_description: Pay the extra, or push back on the upcharge.

title: Structural design is done
story: Structural design is done. I know it took a while — that's what conservative load paths and code review get you. Sit through the presentation. The numbers are sound.
action_description: Watch the presentation. Approve the structure, or send it back.

title: Revised structure, same standards
story: Revised drawings. The changes are subtle — that's how structural revisions work. I'm not redesigning the wheel, I'm tightening the calcs. Compare them properly before you tell me they look the same.
action_description: Compare the new drawings to the old. Accept the revised structure, or send it back again.

title: I'm not signing off until you hear me
story: This one's not yours to call alone. There are pieces of this project I won't budge on — let me tell you which way it's going. You can argue if you want, but you'll lose.
action_description: Hear the owner out. Go with the owner's call, or push back.
outcome_description: The owner's call is locked in.

title: I want to see the finish line
story: Enough back and forth. I want to see this thing finished — here's my call. Take it and move, or come back tomorrow with a better argument.
action_description: Owner's decided fast this round. Go with it, or push for one more round.

title: I cut a corner
story: Owner said get this done at any cost. I'm going to cut a corner. Odds aren't in my favor — I know it.
action_description: Quietly let a contact go for deniability. See if the move lands.
outcome_description: I made my move. Now we see if it stuck.

title: Careful version
story: Last time didn't go well. I'm being a lot more careful this time.
action_description: Quietly part ways with another contact. See how the careful version lands.

title: Department of Buildings counter
story: Department of Buildings. You're here to pay the filing fee — 1% of project value. Standard rate. Sign here, here, and here. We don't haggle on this.
action_description: Pay the fee. Hire a few hands to keep the filing clean.
outcome_description: Fees paid. You're in the system.

title: DOB add-on bill
story: You're back. Add-on fees are owed — review the bill and pay. Once you've paid the original, the add-ons aren't up for debate. We've already done the work on this file.
action_description: Swap a worn-out helper. Pay the extra.

title: I pick my DOB route
story: I'm picking my filing path. Plan Exam is slow but safe. Prof Cert is fast but risky. The owner wants this done — so do I. The call's mine.
action_description: Plan Exam is slower but safer. Prof Cert is faster but riskier. Pick.
outcome_description: Path chosen. I live with it.

title: Waiting in the DOB line
story: Clerks are slow today. Nothing to do but wait — paperwork moves at the line's pace, not mine.
action_description: Hurry up and wait. That's the DOB rhythm.

title: I'm reading your plans
story: I'm working through your plans page by page — every elevation, every section. Checking against code. Nothing personal. If there's an objection, I'll write it up. Save us both time and submit clean.
action_description: Accept the examiner's verdict, or resubmit with revisions.

title: I'm reading the resubmission
story: I'm reading the resubmission. I flip faster on the second pass — I already know what to look for. If you fixed the objections, it'll go quick. If you didn't, it'll go quicker.
action_description: Accept the second read, or resubmit again.

title: Prof Cert filing accepted
story: Prof Cert filing. Self-certified — we barely look. That's the deal you signed up for. Stamp it, file it, you're out the door. Just hope the data entry hand types your numbers right — that's on you, not us.
action_description: File and hope no one checks too hard.

title: You again — second cert
story: You again. Hand it over. Hope your expeditor filled the forms right — at this counter, errors aren't our problem. They're yours.
action_description: File and hope.

title: Auditor's at your file
story: I've pulled your file. ZR-23.5, ZR-25-13, that side yard variance you skipped — I cite them from memory because that's my job. Audits aren't paranoid. They're routine. The findings are yours to accept or contest.
action_description: Read the findings. Accept them, or dispute.

title: Down to the last objections
story: You've cleared most of the objections. A few remain. We'll close them out one of two ways — you accept the final findings, or we have one more conversation. I'd recommend the first.
action_description: Down to the last few. Accept the final call, or push the last few.

title: FDNY intake desk
story: FDNY intake. We deal with what kills people in fires — sprinklers, standpipes, alarms, egress. Don't dance with us. Yes/no questions, straight answers. You hedge, we catch it.
action_description: Answer the routing questions. Be straight — they catch a hedge.

title: FDNY intake, second visit
story: Second visit. We remember faces here. Recognition usually means more attention, not less. Same questions — answer them the same way.
action_description: Run through intake again. Be straight — they remember inconsistencies.

title: FDNY plan exam
story: I read for what kills people in fires. Sprinkler heads, standpipe risers, egress widths, alarm zones. Sound like you know the code if you want — I actually know it. Objections come back specific.
action_description: Accept FDNY's verdict, or push back on objections.

title: FDNY second read — final
story: You've been here once. We don't do third negotiations — this round you get a stamp or you don't. Sit quietly. Speak only when spoken to.
action_description: Approval stamp or denial stamp — which one comes out?

title: Sit down, let's talk price
story: Sit down. You need someone to build this thing — I'm your guy. Quality, cost, schedule — pick two, but I'll be straight with you on all three. Cheap crew costs you on the back end. Good crew costs you up front. Your call.
action_description: Quality and cost multiplier on the table. Sign the contractor, or push back on the price.

title: Change order on the table
story: Look — things shifted on site. Found something we couldn't see in the drawings. I need a change order. Time extension, extra fee. Not unreasonable. But it's not free either.
action_description: Approve the change order, or push back.
try_again_label: Push back on the change order

title: We hit something in the field
story: Boss — we hit something in the field. Wasn't on the drawings. Every hour we're stopped costs you. Need to swap a body in for the right specialist. We can fix it on site if we move now.
action_description: Swap a contact for the right specialist. Try to fix it on site.

title: Another one in the field
story: Boss — another one. Construction sites don't hand you problems one at a time, they pile up. Every day we're slowed costs you. Push hard or eat the delay.
action_description: Push hard to head off the delay. No time to spare.

title: Inspector just walked in
story: Boss — inspector just walked onto the site. Looks fresh, that cuts both ways. There's a safety violation by the southwest corner — let me steer them somewhere else while you handle the paperwork.
action_description: Steer their attention elsewhere. See if it works.

title: Johnes is back for the follow-up
story: Boss — Inspector Johnes is back. He never liked you, but he's fair. Frank's crew just wrapped, two of his guys can join us for the walk. Extra eyes, extra hands. Keep our story straight.
action_description: Walk the site with the inspector. Steady answers, no volunteered info.

title: Final review counter
story: Final review. Birthday party in the back office — everything's running an hour late. You picked a good day to come in. Maybe your file gets a softer read. Maybe.
action_description: Accept the verdict, or ask for another pass.

title: Final review, second pass
story: Bad day at the counter. Supervisor's consoling a clerk who just got chewed out. Files are crawling. Hope nobody notices the photocopy where the original should be.
action_description: Accept the verdict, or ask for another pass.

title: You delivered
story: You delivered. Took longer than I wanted, cost more than I budgeted — but it's done, and it's done right. That's what matters in the end. Good work.
action_description: Final score gets calculated here.

title: Project Complete!
story: You Completed project!
action_description: YOU ARE done! Calculate final score.
